what_happened: Task description's two candidate causes (stdin read in a non-interactive context; unbounded Zotero API/socket wait) were both refuted by a full read of zotero-generate-export.sh and zotero-resolve-sqlite-path.sh: no bare stdin read exists anywhere, and every curl call carries --connect-timeout/--max-time. Actual root cause (confirmed by microbenchmark N=50..2000 showing superlinear growth, and a live uncontended rerun of the failing short-mid-page scenario completing in ~122s) is synthesize_citekeys()'s per-item bash for-loop: each of its ~2828 iterations re-parses the full, growing items_json via a fresh jq subprocess AND re-serializes the full, growing result array via another fresh jq subprocess, giving O(n) subprocess spawns each doing O(n) JSON work -- effectively quadratic wall-clock cost, not a deadlock. Under the isolated timeout 60/90 reproduction this reads as 'stalls past the timeout' (it is killed mid-run, well short of its ~122s uncontended completion time); under the 24-minute concurrent-batch observation (load avg ~40/24 cores) the same mechanism is amplified by severe CPU-scheduling contention across thousands of short-lived jq child processes.

Planning needed no new investigation: reports/02 had already refuted the task description's two hypothesized causes (stdin read, unbounded network wait) with a full source read and localized the real mechanism to synthesize_citekeys()'s per-item jq loop, with a measured microbenchmark and an uncontended 121.7s reproduction. The plan's only extra reads were three confirmations (the single call site, the two generator invocation sites in the test, and that run-all.sh discovers suites from the source store so no deploy step gates Gate 8 coverage).

The suite's curl-stub fixtures carry no author and no issued date and titles of the form 'Item N Title', so every synthesized citekey collides on one base key. That makes the existing fixtures a good collision-path characterization vehicle but leaves author/year/punctuation derivation and pre-existing-citation-key passthrough uncovered by any stub-driven test. Research Recommendation 3 option (b) rules out a test-only hook in the production script, so the plan covers those shapes with a one-time golden diff of the extracted pre-rewrite function in Phase 2 rather than a committed scenario -- a deliberate, documented coverage limit, not an oversight.

Added citekey-synthesis characterization scenario pinning synthesize_citekeys() output (140 items, unique keys, exact ordered base/-2/.../-140 collision sequence) against the unchanged generator, ahead of the Phase 2 bulk-jq rewrite.

Rewrote synthesize_citekeys() in zotero-generate-export.sh as a single bulk jq pass, cutting short-mid-page (2828 items) wall time from ~121.7s to ~6.3s; output verified byte-identical to the pre-rewrite function over an edge-case fixture and the real 140-item fixture.

Wrapped both zotero-generate-export.sh test-suite invocation sites in timeout(60s default), added a shared rc=124 loud-FAIL path, and added a timeout-guard-fires scenario proving the bound fires against a deliberately stalled command. Full 13-scenario suite now completes deterministically in ~12s.

Phase 4 confirmed the fix: the zotero-export suite terminates deterministically (13 scenarios, 0 failed, ~12s wall vs 600s outer bound), run-all.sh's full parallel run shows test-zotero-generate-export.sh passing (no longer the hang source), and the complete verify-deploy.sh gate set now TERMINATES (exit 1, not a hang) at ~1430s, with all 4 remaining gate failures matching pre-existing, task-404-unrelated issues.
